 Orange County election officials see doubleearly voter turnout compared to last midterms
 BY 
 Maggie Rickerby
 Orange County 
 UPDATED 2:01 PM ET Oct. 25, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 9:35 AM ET Oct. 25, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 9:35 AM EDT Oct. 25, 2026 
 SHARE 
 ORLANDO, Fla. — Early voting continues across Central Florida. According to the University of Florida’s Election Lab,over 2.5 million Floridians have already cast their ballots. 
 In Orange County, election officials say the early votes are coming in steady. According to unofficial voter turnout data, over 14,000 showed up to the polls Saturday.
 That number includes mail in ballots. 
 PREVIOUS STORIES:  Early voting across Central Florida counties 
 For more early voting information in your county, visit spectrum News 13's Voter Guide 
 In total, Orange County has seen nearly 147,000 early voters flock to the polls.
 Supervisor of Elections Karen Castor Dentel says voter numbers are averaging around 13,000 a day. 
 “Which is nearly double what the turnout was from four years ago during the last midterm in 2022,” Castor Dentel said.
 Since early voting began on October 19, that first Monday totalled over 19,700 early voters. Friday saw just over 18,000. 
 Those numbers include mail-in ballots as well. 
 Castor Dentel says she’s seen people bring their mail-in ballots in person, which she says could be contributing to higher numbers during this early voting cycle.
 “You can still put them in the mail, you haven’t run out of time yet, but a lot of people are saying they just want to come by and drop it off in person themselves,” Castor Dentel said.
 She said other reasons could be a simple eagerness to vote.
 “People just seem really positive when they get here, it’s a very patriotic experience and I encourage everyone to get out there,” she said.
 Castor Dentel said she can tell many voters have done their research, and many bring their sample ballots in ready to go.
 “They come in, they just bring their sample ballot with all the answers. It's like an open book test and they are easily and quickly filling out their actual ballots and I think that’s really helped reduce any long lines,” she said.
 Out of their 27 voting locations, Castor Dentel says one of the busiest polling places across the board is the Apopka Community Center. 
 But she says lines have remained flowing.
 One challenge Castor Dentel says she's noticed at some of the busier locations, though, is parking.
 She says many of their locations including the John Bridges Community Center, UCF’s Barbara Ying Center and her office on Kaley Street have plenty of parking available.
